PROJECT 3A / MARKET RESEARCH AGENT

Lather Lens

Multi-agent market research
for handmade-soap founders.

What we built: Lather Lens is a web application that helps a founder understand competitors before making product, pricing and marketing decisions, using evidence rather than guesses.

LIVE PILOT - complete - report v4

What this project does

The project uses Petite Batch's India handmade-soap brief as its research scenario. It discovers relevant competitors, gathers dated web and news evidence, examines products, listed prices, ingredients, positioning and sales channels, and produces a source-linked report for human review.

Brief > Discover > Approve shortlist > Research
Analyze > Review > Approve report

LIVE pilot: Fika Soaps and Forest Essentials. Missing SKU/pack details and unsupported opportunities remain explicitly unavailable.

26 October 2026. Actual application screenshots and saved LIVE evidence. No new paid research was run for this document.

01 / HOW THE AGENTS WORK

Reasoning inside
durable boundaries.

Brief → Scout → Human shortlist review
↓
Parallel Researchers → Normalize → Analyst
↓
Independent Reviewer → Bounded correction
↓
Human report approval → Immutable save/export
RoleResponsibility
ScoutTavily discovery, model-assisted relevance, source identity validation; up to three competitors.
ResearcherPublic web/news and first-party product evidence; separate competitor lanes.
AnalystSource-attributed comparison and conditional opportunities. Deterministic arithmetic stays in code.
ReviewerIndependent evidence/arithmetic checks and a separate model critique; unresolved issues block approval.
OrchestratorLangGraph state, checkpoints, retries and human interrupts. Coordination is deterministic.

Stack and model boundary

Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind; FastAPI/Pydantic; SQLAlchemy/Alembic; Supabase Auth/Postgres with owner RLS. A provider-neutral model port isolates the provisional Fireworks configuration. LangSmith remote export is off.

02 / HUMAN CONTROL

A shortlist
you can inspect.

Actual pilot scope

Petite Batch; handmade cold-process soap; India. Fika Soaps and Forest Essentials passed discovery checks and were explicitly approved by the user. The system retained the reason for fewer than three candidates.

Use the local application

  1. Open the signed-in project browser with node scripts/open-local.cjs --live --report.
  2. Inspect Shortlist, Live Run and Report for this same run.
  3. Review the AI briefing, limitations and clickable evidence.
  4. Approve only a report you accept; then download HTML/CSV after saved state.

The local session helper uses the existing disposable local identity. Keys and tokens are never included in the submission. Hosting is not required by the supplied handout.

03 / EVIDENCE AND RECOVERY

Show the work.
Keep the unknowns.

04 / REPORT QUALITY AND SUBMISSION

Claims need more
than a citation.

A valid URL and intact quote establish traceability, not entailment. The independent model reviewer can flag wrong prices, dates and unsupported wording, but genuine support still requires claim-level adjudication. Unknown SKU/pack bindings prevent price-per-100g arithmetic.

Acceptance and limitations

  • Original BRD: at least 90% material-claim traceability; at least 4/5 owner-rated useful reports; at least 4/5 failure tests handled; resume without losing completed work; no knowingly fabricated facts.
  • Owner usefulness and full real-claim support remain unmeasured. Offline test passes are separate from business acceptance.
  • Model benchmark design exists; final model selection is not complete.
  • Website restrictions, missing SKU/weights and stale announcements remain visible. No external publishing or deployment has occurred.

Submission: clean source repository/ZIP, this illustrated overview, a four-minute walkthrough and the approved sourced sample. Preserve historical documents locally; exclude secrets, caches and account screenshots.

06 / FRAMEWORKS, ARCHITECTURE AND APIS

How the application
fits together.

Browser: Next.js / TypeScript / Tailwind
↓ same-origin server routes + private session cookie
FastAPI / Pydantic → owner authorization
↓
Harness: allowlists / approval / budget / evidence / replay
↓
LangGraph worker → Scout / Researcher / Analyst / Reviewer
↙ Tavily + model adapter    ↘ Supabase Postgres
LayerWhat we used and why
InterfaceNext.js App Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS; Brief, Shortlist, Live Run, Report and History.
BackendPython FastAPI and Pydantic typed requests/results; SQLAlchemy repositories and Alembic migrations.
State and identitySupabase Auth and Postgres; owner RLS, durable checkpoints, fenced worker lease and heartbeat, immutable report versions.
Search APITavily Search API through the harness only; public HTTPS retrieval validates destinations, redirects and access restrictions.
Model APIProvider-neutral ModelAdapter port. The authorized pilot uses Fireworks JSON chat with Kimi K3 provisionally. Keys stay server-side; no final benchmark winner.
ObservabilityPersisted event journal and sanitized LangSmith integration. Remote LangSmith export is disabled.
Validationpytest, Ruff, mypy; Vitest, ESLint, TypeScript; Playwright screenshots and 17 deterministic golden cases.

Application API examples

POST /api/briefs saves a brief; GET /api/workspace reads persisted results; shortlist/report decision routes record version-bound approval; the run export route returns approved HTML/CSV. FastAPI publishes OpenAPI schemas. No API key is exposed to the browser.

This submission runs locally. No cloud deployment, hosted production capacity or final business acceptance pass is claimed.
